The theories of general relativity and quantum mechanics are both fundamental pillars of modern physics, yet they differ significantly in their scope and current compatibility. General relativity addresses gravity and the large-scale structure of the universe, whereas quantum mechanics explains particle behavior at the smallest scales. While both are essential for understanding the universe, they are currently incompatible with each other under certain extreme conditions, such as inside black holes or at the moment of the Big Bang.
